name: Friendsgiving at Megan and Chris's place

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: Hi everyone, I'm Megan Walsh. I'm a pediatric nurse at Children's Hospital, and this is my house, so welcome to Friendsgiving.

lines.speaker: Chris Porter
lines.text: I'm Chris Porter, Megan's husband. I'm an accountant at Deloitte, and I play keyboard in a band on the weekends.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: I'm Nina Shah. I teach high school chemistry here in Denver, and I moved out from Chicago a few years ago.

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: Hey, I'm Owen Brooks. I'm a physical therapist, and I spend most of my free time climbing.

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: I'm Hannah Kim. I'm a lawyer at a small firm downtown, and I just got engaged.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: And I'm Ben Carter. I teach music at a high school, and I sing in the band Chris just mentioned.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: Okay, before anyone touches the turkey, Hannah, show everyone the ring.

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: Fine, fine. Here it is. Tyler proposed last month in Sedona, at sunrise, at the top of a red rock trail. I was sweaty and I had no makeup on.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: No way! It's gorgeous.

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: Congrats, Hannah. Seriously. Tyler is a good guy.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: Wait, is it weird that Owen is the first one to congratulate you?

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: Ha, not at all. Owen and I dated for almost five years, but that ended in 2021, and honestly we are way better as friends.

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: We met at the climbing gym in 2016. She fell off an easy route and landed right on top of me. That was our meet cute.

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: I slipped. There is a difference.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: And now you two are still in the same climbing crew. The Sunday Sends, right?

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: Yep. Me, Hannah, Sam Torres, and Kevin Doyle. Every Sunday morning at the gym in Golden, and then breakfast burritos after.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Tyler doesn't climb though, does he?

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: Tyler Grant does not climb. Tyler Grant watches golf on television. We are working on it.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: Ha, true.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Okay, Megan, Chris, you have to tell the Bonnaroo story. I've only ever heard pieces of it.

lines.speaker: Chris Porter
lines.text: Alright. So it's Bonnaroo, June 2015, in Tennessee, and it's about a hundred degrees. My tent collapses on the very first night because I set it up on a slope, like an idiot. And the girl in the tent next to mine just walks over with a mallet and a bag of extra stakes, and rebuilds the whole thing in ten minutes without saying a single word. That was Megan.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: He was holding the instructions upside down. I couldn't watch.

lines.speaker: Chris Porter
lines.text: Then we ended up at the same show that night, and she recognized me as the tent guy. We spent the rest of the weekend together. After that we flew back and forth between Denver and Nashville for about a year, until she finally moved out here.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: And four years later we got married in Asheville. October 2019. It poured rain for the whole ceremony.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: I officiated that wedding, by the way. I got ordained online for twenty dollars.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Wait, Ben, how do you and Megan know each other?

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: Megan is my cousin. Our moms are sisters. We grew up two streets apart in Ohio.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: He used to steal my bike. Every single summer.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: Borrow. I borrowed it.

lines.speaker: Chris Porter
lines.text: Ben is also the one who got me into the band. The Late Shift.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: Right, so the band is me on vocals and guitar, Rob Hayes on bass, Danny Cruz on drums, and Chris on keyboard. Rob and I started it back in college. We met in the jazz ensemble in 2010, and we've been playing bars around Denver ever since. We have a gig at the Bluebird in January, if anyone wants to come.

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: I'll be there.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Ben, is that the scar from the car accident? On your arm?

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: Yeah. That was 2012. I was driving back from a gig in Boulder, it was snowing, and a pickup truck slid right through a red light and hit my passenger side. I broke my arm in two places, and I couldn't play guitar for six months.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: Ben, that was 2013. I was in nursing school. I remember coming to the hospital between exams.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: No, it was definitely 2012. It was the winter before I graduated.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: I'm telling you, it was 2013. I have a photo of your cast somewhere.

lines.speaker: Chris Porter
lines.text: I am staying out of this one.

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: So, Nina, how long have you been in Denver now?

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: I moved here from Chicago in 2018. No wait, it was 2019. Right after the school year ended, that summer.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: And then you joined the book club.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Yes! Second Chapter. That's actually how Megan and I met, in 2020, on a video call during lockdown.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: It's me, Nina, Laura Bennett, and Emily Hart. We read one book a month, and mostly we drink wine.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Laura and I went to college together. She's the one who got me into it.

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: What are you reading right now?

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Something very sad about a lighthouse. Emily picked it, obviously.

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: Megan, didn't you say your brother was coming?

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: Andrew Walsh, yes, my little brother. He's driving down from Fort Collins, and he is always late.

lines.speaker: Chris Porter
lines.text: And my coworker Andrew Collins might stop by too. He just moved here from Boston and doesn't know anyone yet, so I invited him.

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: Two Andrews. Got it.

lines.speaker: Chris Porter
lines.text: Andrew Collins and I sit next to each other at Deloitte. He's the one who taught me to snowboard last winter.

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: Oh, I owe Andrew twenty dollars from the Broncos game. Remind me when he gets here.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: Speaking of food, can we please eat? The turkey has been resting for like an hour.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Okay, this stuffing is incredible. Who made this?

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: That's me. My grandma's recipe. A lot of sausage.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: Owen and I work together at Children's Hospital. He started there in 2019, and he's the only physical therapist the kids actually like.

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: That's because I let them race wheelchairs down the hallway. Last spring I had a twelve year old recovering from knee surgery, a really quiet kid, and he wouldn't do any of his exercises. So I told him, if you do all your reps for a week, we race. He did every single one. On Friday we raced down the third floor hallway, he beat me by a mile, and a surgeon came around the corner and nearly got run over.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: I was the one who had to write the incident report.

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: That's amazing.

lines.speaker: Chris Porter
lines.text: So, are we doing the Thanksgiving thing where everyone says what they're grateful for?

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Ugh, fine. I'm grateful I finally passed my car inspection.

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: I'm grateful for Tyler, obviously. And for Owen, for not making this weird.

lines.speaker: Owen Brooks
lines.text: I'm grateful nobody fell on me at the gym this year.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: I'm grateful for my arm, which works fine now, no thanks to that pickup truck in 2012.

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: Okay, my turn. I'm grateful for all of you. When I moved out here for Chris in 2016, I didn't know a single person in Denver except him. And now I've got the book club, I've got band nights, and I've got Hannah and Owen dragging me to the climbing gym even though I hate it. This table is my whole family out here.

lines.speaker: Nina Shah
lines.text: Stop, you're going to make me cry.

lines.speaker: Chris Porter
lines.text: And I'm grateful that Megan knows how to pitch a tent.

lines.speaker: Ben Carter
lines.text: Has anyone heard from Andrew? Should we save him a plate?

lines.speaker: Megan Walsh
lines.text: Save him two. He's always starving.

lines.speaker: Hannah Kim
lines.text: Okay, somebody pass the pie.

events.name: Megan and Chris's wedding in Asheville
Hannah and Tyler's engagement in Sedona
